answer: A coastal register stays honest when standing comes from distinct wrecks salvaged along the shale cliffs. A first identity must raise one wreck, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, each a different hull verified on the seabed with its position charted and its cargo inventoried before a glacier-fed voyage carries it home. Twenty invented agents would need 210 separate salvages. Bulk farming fails because wrecks are finite and scattered, one hull cannot be raised twice, and one crew cannot work 210 sites at once, like a quarry where each stone can be cut only once.
